title: Should <select>'s first child <button> be able to submit or reset the form?
body:
The content model of `select` allows a first child `button` element, and the `button` element's "Contexts in which this element can be used" says "As the first child of a `select` element". Neither restricts the `type` attribute, so `<select><button type=submit>` and `<select><button type=reset>` are conforming.

[Submit button](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#concept-submit-button):

> A `button` element is said to be a submit button if any of the following are true:
>
> * the `type` attribute is in the Auto state, both the `command` and `commandfor` content attributes are not present, and the parent node is not a `select` element; or
> * the `type` attribute is in the Submit Button state.

The `select` carve-out is only in the first bullet, so a first child `button` with `type=submit` *is* a submit button. Such a button is [inert](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-button-element), which stops the user from activating it, but inertness does not stop:

* `button.click()`, which runs the activation behavior and submits the form; or
* the button becoming the form's default button and being activated by implicit submission from, say, a text field elsewhere in the form.

`type=reset` has the same shape: it is not a submit button, but its activation behavior still resets the form, and inertness does not prevent that either.

So the first child `button` of a `select` can submit or reset the form after all, which seems contrary to the intent. Options:

1. Extend the carve-out so that a `button` whose parent is a `select` is never a submit button, and does not reset either, whatever its `type`.
2. Make `type` non-conforming on a `select`'s first child `button`.
3. Decide this is fine, since the author explicitly opted in by writing `type`.

Noticed while fixing the note after the customizable select example, which claimed "Its form submission behavior is prevented because it is inert." That is not the mechanism — not being a submit button is — and it does not hold when `type` is specified.
